notes: causality verified by this reviewer, not taken on trust: copying main:internal/proxy/k8s_notify.go over HEAD makes TestNotifyScanGivesEachRegisteredClusterItsOwnBudget fail with `sent:1 resources:1 truncated:true` — exactly the claimed symptom (c-busy's two newer rows eat the shared window, c-quiet's privileged pod is never evaluated). Tree restored, `git status --porcelain` empty. go build ./..., go vet ./internal/proxy, gofmt -l on both touched files, and go test ./... -count=1 all clean.

internal/proxy/k8s_notify.go:296-316 (quiet hours) — behaviour cost the implementer disclosed, confirmed: on main the events/revisions lookups sat AFTER the quiet-hours early return, so a scan inside the quiet window cost 1 inventory query. It now costs 3 x registered-cluster-count queries plus all three windows materialised in memory, then discards them at line 315. No observable output change (the quiet response builds its own map and never carries the window fields, and no new error path aborts), so this is pure waste, not a wrong answer — but a 5-minute cron on a 50-cluster fleet does ~150 throwaway queries per quiet-hour tick. ideas.json already carries it; worth keeping it at the top of that list.

internal/proxy/k8s_notify.go:337-339 — the fanout removes the only bound this endpoint had on analyzer input: items is now up to notifyScanBudget x N and events up to 500 x N. analyzer/rca.go:70-71 falls back to workloadRelatedEvents(item, events) for every Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet with no exactly-keyed event (the common case, since events key on Pods), and that is O(events) per item -> O(N^2) overall. Order of magnitude: ~200 workloads x 20 clusters against 10k events is ~4e7 substring scans (seconds); 50 clusters is ~2.5e8 (tens of seconds), alongside 2000 x N full Spec blobs resident at once. HTTP_WRITE_TIMEOUT defaults to 10 minutes (config.go:426) so nothing gets cut off, and AnalyzeSecurity (security.go:107,113) is linear — so this is headroom being spent, not a break. Not demanding a rewrite, but the shape that keeps both properties is available: run AnalyzeRCA/EnrichWithConfigChanges/AnalyzeSecurity and notify inside the per-target loop and release each cluster's rows, since no analyzer correlates across clusters (rcaKey is cluster-scoped) and GetK8sNamespaceOwner is already cluster-scoped. Author's call.

internal/proxy/k8s_notify.go:192-195 — a ListK8sClusters failure returns []string{""} and the response then looks identical to a genuinely-empty registry: clusters_scanned:1, no error field, no notice. That is the same silent-degradation shape this change exists to fix, and it is inconsistent with the events_error/revisions_error treatment two blocks down. Narrow in practice (a DB that cannot serve ListK8sClusters will 500 on the very next ListK8sInventory at line 253), so notes rather than a reject — but a clusters_error field would close it.

internal/proxy/k8s_notify.go:292-294 — in the unregistered fallback the single target is "", so a truncated fallback scan emits clusters_truncated:[""]. Harmless (key-wise assertions, per the repo's scan-response convention) but reads as a bug to an operator. TestNotifyScanFallsBackToASingleWindowWithoutRegisteredClusters does not pin it either way.

internal/proxy/k8s_notify.go:275-277,285-287 — eventsError/revisionsError keep only the first failing cluster; with ten clusters failing, nine are invisible. window_notice still fires, so the operator is not told a clean story. Documented in docs/K8S_OPERATIONS_HUB.md; acceptable, worth knowing.

release note, not a defect: the first fleet-wide scan after this ships evaluates clusters that were previously never reached, so every standing privileged workload and over-broad Role in them pages at once (each with a fresh 6h dedup window). That burst is the fix working, but an operator who is not warned will read it as a regression. Also: findings from newly-reached namespaces with no k8s_namespace_ownership row route to the default webhook rather than a team channel — pre-existing routing, newly visible.

no security finding: no new route, authorizeAdmin at line 223 unchanged, no auth/secret/crypto code touched. Target IDs come from the k8s_clusters registry rather than from request input, both ingest paths (admin_k8s.go:428, admin_k8s_agent.go:500) already 404 inventory for unregistered clusters, and DeleteK8sCluster (store/k8s.go:387-419) cascades k8s_inventory/k8s_events/k8s_resource_revisions — so the fanout's target set is neither attacker-steerable nor narrower than the window it replaces. Scope is unchanged too: a fleet scan already read every cluster's rows via an unfiltered query, so nothing is widened. Per-cluster GetK8sNamespaceOwner keeps channel routing cluster-scoped, so no cross-cluster leak into Mattermost.

no legal/privacy finding: no new category of data is collected, stored or transmitted. The two added fields (clusters_scanned, clusters_truncated) are operational cluster identifiers in an admin-only response and the existing audit entry; no personal data, no new vendor, no retention or transfer change, no external commitment in the docs text.

revert is clean — three files, no schema change, no migration, no config or flag added, no external state written. The only residue of a run is k8s notification dedup rows claimed for clusters that are now reached, and those expire on the existing 6h window.

still unverified, as always in this repo: real PostgreSQL, real Kubernetes, and real fleet size. The scaling numbers above are arithmetic over the budgets, not measurements — nobody has run this against an actual multi-cluster install, and the implementer was right to flag that the registered-cluster-count distribution is unknown.
